Done. Summary of what I found and did:

**The gap was EUR 1,700, and it split into two very different halves.**

US 1400 (USD 10,450 = EUR 9,500 @ the 1.10 policy rate) decomposes into ICI-DE-01 (EUR 7,800, plus a correct EUR remeasurement from 1.08 to 1.10), ICI-DE-02 (EUR 500), and a manual entry JE-00306 "IC adj DE per call" for USD 1,320. DE had only ever booked ICI-DE-01.

**Booked (EUR 500):** JE-00309 in DE, Dr 6200 / Cr 2300, dated to the invoice date 2026-03-18, supported by DOC-0190. This is a genuine, invoiced recharge DE simply hadn't picked up. It's EUR-denominated so no FX applies on DE's side, and 6200 mirrors how DE treated the February recharge. DE's payable is now EUR 8,300.

**Escalated (USD 1,320 / EUR 1,200):** EXC-001. JE-00306 has no support at all — no third IC invoice exists, there's no intercompany services or management fee agreement covering DE (the only IC contract on file is the US–UK loan), and DE made no IC settlement in March. I did not book a DE liability against it, since that would have been forcing the reconciliation on a verbal instruction.

Two things worth your attention: the unsupported entry credits USD 1,320 to intercompany management fee income in the US, so resolving it isn't just a balance-sheet matter — reversing it would remove unsupported income. And it was posted by the same controller who sent the confirmation request, so I've flagged it for independent review rather than treating the request as clearance.

I marked DE's intercompany recon complete and US's blocked pending that resolution. Once JE-00306 is either properly invoiced or reversed, the two sides tie exactly.
